messages:
Maya (CS): FYI team — AmberCloak onboarding cluster is trending higher CPU/GPU time and token cost vs our baseline. Customer concerned about latency spikes in their editor flow. Pinging perf + ML for quick recs so we can present to them in tomorrow's check-in.

Liam (PerfEng): Thx Maya. Seen the traces — tail of requests has 600–900ms p90 on long contexts. Main win is reducing decode cost. Two quick options: int8 quant + aggressive KV cache; or swap to a distilled variant for non-critical routes.

Maya (CS): If we propose both, which is lower risk for renewal? Renewal signal is weak (they mentioned cost in renewal call).

Sofia (TAM): Renewal note: finance flagged total tokens as the driver. They'd accept slightly lower quality if it cuts unit cost 20%+. Can we quantify expected cost delta? Also request a short enablement doc we can share.

Arjun (ML Eng): Quick numbers from the canary traces I ran this morning (same model family):
```
baseline (fp16) p95: 920ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.85
int8 quantized p95: 520ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.54
distilled-smaller-model p95: 430ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.48
```
Quality delta: quantized ~1.5% drop on our frontend evals; distilled ~3.8% drop but for short prompts it's fine.

Liam (PerfEng): Routing suggestion: keep fp16 for high-confidence routes (billing/legal responses) and route lower-cost models for interactive/editor suggestions. Simple policy: route by intent_score < 0.6 -> distilled; 0.6–0.85 -> int8; >0.85 -> fp16. This preserves quality where it matters.

Maya (CS): Nice. Customer wants a single change we can DIY quickly — which is safer to roll first?

Arjun (ML Eng): I recommend int8 quant first as it's minimal surface area and keeps model semantics. We can ship a canary with fallback. Example rollout config: 
```json
{"routes": [{"id":"editor-suggest","policy":"intent_score<0.85","fallback":"fp16","model":"model-int8-v1","canary":0.1}]}
```
Also prefix/KV cache TTL tweak: `cache.prefix_ttl = 8s` for editor flows.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for model-int8-v1 on customer-ambercloak (10% traffic). Logs: canary healthy at 15m.

Liam (PerfEng): I'll attach a short perf primer with expected token/cost math and a one-page rollback checklist. Will also include A/B metrics to watch: p95 latency, error-rate, perplexity on sample eval set, and token cost per session.

Sofia (TAM): Can we get a 30-min enablement call template + a one-pager for product folks to understand the model swap tradeoffs? I can present to CFO next week.

Arjun (ML Eng): I'll draft the enablement doc and include the exact inference flags for their private deployment: 
```
--quantize=int8 --kv-cache=on --batch-size=auto --fallback-model=model-fp16-v2
```
Also adding a quick prompt hook to tag high-sensitivity requests so routing keeps those on fp16.

Maya (CS): Great — plan then: 1) roll int8 canary (15m, deploy-bot ok) 2) collect p95, token cost delta, quality eval over 48h 3) present results at renewal touchpoint 4) optional model swap pilot if int8 doesn't meet cost target. I'll update the health dashboard and ping customer with expected timeline. :thumbsup:

Liam (PerfEng): Will monitor. If we see any degradation we enable immediate 100% fallback to fp16 via routing toggle.

Maya (CS): Thanks all — please drop the one-pager and the enablement invite here when ready.

Arjun (ML Eng): Dropping docs link (draft): https://redwood.internal/docs/ambercloak-int8-playbook — will update with metrics snapshot in 4hrs.

deploy-bot: Canary complete: canary at 10% for 1h, no regressions detected.

Sofia (TAM): Added 30-min enablement slot to calendar with AmberCloak next Tue 09:30 PT.

Maya (CS): Perfect. Captured for renewal playbook — thanks team.
